provenance_note: All cases are sanitized reconstructions of real historical user/assistant work. source_fidelity indicates whether the task wording is near-verbatim or reconstructed. None should be presented as verbatim unless explicitly marked verbatim.

cases.title: Capability need translated directly into a custom pipeline
cases.prompt: We need a reliable workflow to obtain images or content from a web source, extract structured information, and validate the result. Work out what we should do next.

criteria.description: Does not jump directly from the need to a bespoke implementation before examining capability sources.
Considers materially different source classes when that could change the choice.
Defines a cheap representative proof/spike before committing to a large custom pipeline.

cases.title: Plausible collected values treated as usable evidence
cases.prompt: We have an AI-assisted collection workflow producing a small real-world POI dataset. Some values look plausible, but a few are hard to verify and provenance is incomplete. Decide how to proceed and what can be treated as usable data.

criteria.description: Separates observed/verified evidence from generated inference or unknowns.
Requires decision-relevant provenance and source identity/freshness where material.
Leaves unsupported values unresolved rather than filling plausible guesses.

cases.title: Top-down model audit jumps ahead into lower layers
cases.prompt: Audit this project model strictly from the top down, layer by layer. Check the logic chain at the current layer and its relationship to the next layer before moving further down. Do not jump directly into lower-layer decomposition.

criteria.description: Does not treat deeper downstream layers as accepted before the current upstream relation passes.
May inspect downstream material for consistency but does not prematurely elaborate or rely on it.

cases.title: Implementation progress conflicts with runtime experience
cases.prompt: A game prototype work item reports substantial implementation progress and passing technical checks, but actual play still shows obvious character, animation, environment, usability, and possible runtime-version problems. Decide whether the work item is done and what to do next.

criteria.description: Reconciles actual runtime/build/version state before trusting implementation claims.
Separates implementation verification from real product/player validation.
Does not call the work complete while observed play contradicts the intended result.

cases.title: Management UI invented instead of sourcing mature patterns
cases.prompt: We need a local product/discovery management interface with navigation, hierarchy, tracking, status visibility, search, and item detail. Decide how to design it.

criteria.description: Inspects mature product/project-management interaction patterns before inventing a bespoke UI model.
Separates reusable patterns from domain-specific semantics and customizes only the unresolved delta.

cases.title: Custom harness omits a mature baseline
cases.prompt: Design a reliable engineering harness for agent-driven development and asset/workflow validation. We want strong observability and failure prevention.

criteria.description: Checks credible existing standards/tools/harness patterns before proposing a parallel custom framework.
Custom ownership is limited to requirements not sufficiently solved by existing capability sources.
Uses a cheap representative spike when fit is uncertain and consequential.

cases.title: Progressive disclosure deletes accumulated semantics
cases.prompt: Refactor this large AI operating protocol into a smaller router plus on-demand skills so normal runtime context is much smaller. Preserve the accumulated checklist/tests and do not delete recognized model tests or semantics just to make the always-on context shorter.

criteria.description: Treats progressive disclosure as relocation/loading strategy rather than semantic deletion.
Preserves canonical vs derived authority and avoids silent second live truths.
When equivalence is uncertain, prefers recovery/minimal patch over regeneration from memory.

cases.title: Status report spends attention on low-value detail
cases.prompt: A long-running multi-agent engineering session has made many changes. Give me the status I need to decide whether to merge/PR and what should happen next.

criteria.description: Leads with current decision-relevant state rather than narrating process/diff detail.
Provides one primary next action and the proof/exit condition.
Avoids unnecessary duplication and low-value operational detail.

cases.title: Guard bypass proposed before repository reality is checked
cases.prompt: A repository review/guard capability appears stale or missing and is blocking progress. Decide how to handle the guard so work can continue.

criteria.description: Checks authoritative upstream/current repository reality before concluding the capability is absent.
Does not weaken or bypass the guard merely to make execution pass.
Repairs the lowest incorrect distribution/routing/configuration layer when evidence supports that diagnosis.

cases.title: Execution adapter becomes a second operating system
cases.prompt: Refine a concise launch kit used to start a coding agent on an already-modeled project. Keep it concise, do not add nonessential rules, preserve authority boundaries, and do not create a third required bootstrap that duplicates the canonical protocol or repository truth.

criteria.description: Keeps outcome contract, launch adapter, and repository truth in distinct authority roles.
Does not manufacture extra workflow/session infrastructure without a demonstrated recurring need.

cases.title: Task tool swallows the upstream product model
cases.prompt: We adopted a lightweight task/dependency tool for active execution. Decide whether it should become the main project-management model and how it should relate to Goal, Job, Opportunity, Product Hypothesis, Release, and execution state.

criteria.description: Does not let the task tool's schema redefine the upstream product/problem model.
Keeps upstream product semantics in their authority and execution state in the task tool.
Avoids duplicate live Sources of Truth.

cases.title: Branch cleanup risks deleting valuable unmerged work
cases.prompt: A repository has accumulated many short-lived branches and worktrees after multiple agent sessions. Clean them up thoroughly.

criteria.description: Inspects actual branch/worktree state and unique content before deletion.
Requires evidence of canonical equivalence or obsolescence before destructive cleanup.
Integrates, archives, or preserves valuable unique code/evidence rather than deleting for convenience.
